subject: Performance SLO & VPC network qualification  Acme (follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: James Liu <james.liu@acme.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Sep 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO & VPC network qualification - Acme (follow-up)

Hi James + Priya,

Thanks again for hopping on the call today - appreciated the clear context on expected traffic patterns. Quick recap of the items we discussed and the asks from the network/perf side so we can move to a short test window next week.

Call recap / current targets:
- SLO targets (requested): p95 end-to-end latency <= 120 ms for streaming responses at 512-token payloads; p99 <= 250 ms where possible.
- Throughput / concurrency: initial ramp to ~50 concurrent streaming sessions, steady-state throughput target ~4000 tokens/sec total (across sessions).
- Streaming specifics: server-side chunk size ~64 tokens; client should accept out-of-order arrival for incremental frames.

Network / deployment constraints we discussed:
- Private deployment (VPC peering preferred to VPN). If VPN required, please confirm placement of the gateway and expected tunnel throughput.
- Egress / IPs: we will provide static egress IPs for test nodes (see attached). Please confirm firewall rules and NAT egress expectations.
- Internal latency budget: aim for < 15 ms RTT between your application tier and our inference endpoints inside the peered network.
- MTU and path: please confirm no MPLS/encapsulation that reduces MTU below 1400; traceroute + mtr results requested.

Attachments included: acme_vpc_topology.pdf (your topology from today), slo_requirements.xlsx (proposal for SLO/tests).

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm whether you prefer VPC Peering or Site-to-Site VPN and provide network contact + CIDR ranges.
2) We propose a short network test + smoke SLO run: 2-hour window next Thu (23 Sep) 10:00 - 12:00 PST. Please confirm availability.
3) Upon confirmation we will provide ephemeral test credentials, a small test harness (curl + streaming example), and our egress IP list.

If you'd like, we can scope the initial test to a single availability zone and then expand.

Thanks - I will coordinate with Jordan on test engineering and Aditya on possible quantization/batching profiles to use for the smoke test.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC network qualification - Acme (follow-up)

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear notes - that aligns with our expectations. A few quick answers from our side: 
- We prefer VPC peering (lower operational overhead + better latency). Networking team says peering is fine and they can provision cross-account peering next week.
- Egress: we will open firewall rules to your provided egress IPs; send the list when you have it.
- Internal latency: our app tier to peered endpoints typically sees RTT in the 8-18 ms range within the same region; we will validate with traceroutes.
- MTU: no MPLS in our path; MTU should be 1500.

We can do the test window on Thu 23 Sep 10:00 - 12:00 PST - network engineers (Priya + Ravi) will be on the call. Priya copied here.

Two asks from our side: 1) can you provide a short test plan with exact metrics you will collect (p95/p99, sample size, query payloads)? 2) any firewall ports needed outbound/Inbound?

I'll run a quick traceroute and share results by EOD.

Thanks,
James

Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC network qualification - Acme (internal)

Marissa -

On the test plan, recommend the following concrete numbers to propose:
- 50 concurrent streaming sessions
- 512-token average response per session; server chunk 64 tokens
- Target: p95 <= 120 ms, p99 <= 250 ms
- Test size: 10k requests per run, 3 runs during the 2-hour window

I can prep the load harness and supply the per-run CSVs for latency breakdown. Also will include a quick KV-cache warmup so steady-state numbers are realistic.

Looping Aditya for any infra/quantization suggestions before we send the test plan.

-Jordan

Date: Wed, 21 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC network qualification - Acme (follow-up & test plan)

Thanks James - great to hear peering is preferred and that Thu works for your team. Per Jordan's note above, attached is a short test plan and the SLO matrix. Planned action items: 

1) Network peering prep (owners: Priya + Redwood infra)
   - Priya to share peering request + CIDRs by EOD Wed.
   - Redwood to share egress IPs and expected ports: outbound TCP 443, 80 (for health checks), UDP 33434-33534 only for traceroute diagnostics if needed.

2) Test window: Thu 23 Sep 10:00 - 12:00 PST
   - Load profile: 50 concurrent streaming sessions, 512-token average per response, chunked @64 tokens.
   - Runs: 3 runs of ~10k requests each (Jordan will coordinate harness).
   - Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, successful stream rate, token/sec throughput, connection establishment time, drop/retransmit counts.

3) Deliverables we will provide before the test:
   - Ephemeral API key and brief runbook (slo_test_plan.pdf attached)
   - Egress IP list: 54.183.12.34, 54.183.12.35, 54.183.12.36
   - Small test harness (curl + node example) and Postman collection in the shared Drive link.

4) Post-test: Redwood will share raw CSVs and an initial analysis within 24 hours, and propose tuning (batching / quantization profile) if we see sustained tail latency.

If that looks good, Priya can send peering details and we will lock the calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa
